title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is enumerating 'MD-graphes', the dual graphs of maximally degenerate stable curves, whose modular dimension is zero. In such a graph every vertex is a 3-pointed rational component (M_{0,3}), so for each vertex v, degree(v) + weight(v) = 3. A loop counts 2 toward the degree, and the weight is the number of marked points on that component. The 'dimension modulaire ambiante' of such a graph is dim M_{g,ν} = 3(g-1)+ν with g = h_1(G). He wants all MD-graphs of ambient dimension ≤ 2, i.e. the maximally degenerate points of the moduli spaces of dimension ≤ 2. These are the 'first two levels' of the Teichmüller tower in the sense of the Esquisse d'un programme. The previous page did the case h_1 = 0, i.e. trees, where 3 ≤ ν ≤ 5. That gives one 3-pointed vertex (M_{0,3}), the segment 2—2 (M_{0,4}) and the chain 2—1—2 (M_{0,5}). This page does case b), h_1 = 1. Here the ambient dimension is 3(1-1)+ν = ν, so ν ≤ 2. Ends (degree-1 vertices) must carry weight 2, so ν ≤ 2 allows at most one end, and every other vertex then has order 3. Topologically, a connected graph with h_1 = 1 and exactly one end is a circle with a tail (a 'lollipop'). Any degree-2 vertex would carry weight 1 and push ν above 2. So there are no degree-2 vertices, and G is the combinatorial lollipop: a loop vertex joined to an end vertex of weight 2. With no end, G is homeomorphic to a circle. All its vertices then have order 2 and weight 1, and there must be at least one vertex, so there are 1 or 2 such vertices. Result (65): (i) one vertex with a loop and weight 1: ν = 1, the irreducible nodal rational curve in \bar M_{1,1}. (ii) Two weight-1 vertices joined by two edges: ν = 2, two P^1's meeting in two points, each carrying one marked point (the 'banana' curve in \bar M_{1,2}). (iii) A loop vertex joined to a weight-2 vertex: ν = 2, a nodal rational curve with a P^1 tail carrying both marked points (in \bar M_{1,2}). The marginal sketches draw the corresponding degenerate curves with their marked points a, b. Together with the three tree cases, this gives the six MD-graphs of ambient dimension ≤ 2. They are the maximally degenerate 'base points at infinity' of M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, M_{1,1} and M_{1,2}. The next page computes their automorphism groups Γ and the subgroups Γ^! fixing the marked points, and interprets these as automorphism groups of the universal curve with 'épiphragme'. These are the data needed for a two-level (Lego/Teichmüller) presentation of the Teichmüller tower at infinity.
errors: He writes 0 ≤ ν ≤ 2, but ν = 0 is impossible: g = 1, ν = 0 is unstable, and he himself notes that at least one marked vertex is needed. So the effective range is 1 ≤ ν ≤ 2. This is a harmless slip.
Equation numbering clash: this page labels the h_1 = 1 list (65), while the next page reuses (65) for the tree list and (66) for this list.

ideas.what: Classification of maximally degenerate stable (dual) graphs, with every vertex a 3-pointed rational component, whose ambient moduli space has dimension ≤ 2. For h_1 = 1 there are exactly three: one in \bar M_{1,1} and two in \bar M_{1,2}.
ideas.modern_name: 0-dimensional boundary strata (pants decompositions / maximal multicurves) of \bar M_{1,1} and \bar M_{1,2}; trivalent stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard stable-graph combinatorics (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen). The low-dimensional base-point lists appear in the Lego/Teichmüller-tower literature (Hatcher–Thurston; Moore–Seiberg; Bakalov–Kirillov; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura–Schneps).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) states the two-level principle and lists the relevant M_{g,ν} of modular dimension ≤ 2. Unsure whether this explicit graph enumeration appears there.

ideas.what: Using ambient modular dimension 3(h_1 - 1) + ν with the vertex balance 'degree + weight = 3' to bound graph shapes. Ends need weight 2, so few marked points force at most one end and a topological classification (circle or lollipop).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine enumeration of the three maximally degenerate genus-one curves in \bar M_{1,1} and \bar M_{1,2}. It serves the Esquisse two-level programme and is well known in the Teichmüller-tower/Lego literature. Only the terminology ('MD-graphes', 'dimension modulaire ambiante', 'épiphragme' on the next page) is idiosyncratic.
transcription_corrections: 'donc dimension G = ν' should read 'donc dim_amb G = ν' (ambient modular dimension). In (65), 'dimension G' should likewise read 'dim. amb. G' ('dimamb G' in the image).

The passage after 'homéomorphe au cercle' reads approximately: 'Dans ce cas tous ses sommets sont d'ordre 2, donc de poids marqués 1, le nombre de ces sommets (donc marqués 1) est 1 ou 2 (il doit y avoir au moins un sommet), on a [cercle à un sommet] et [cercle à deux sommets].'
The ending reads 'En tout on trouve donc trois cas nouveaux :'.
'et s'il n'y a pas' was corrected to 'et si G n'a pas de sommets d'ordre 2'.
'graphe topologiquement connexe' is an insertion above 'graphe avec h_1 = 1'.
